I saved for that trip for two years, and I am going to tell you exactly how, because everybody asks and nobody believes the answer. I did not stop buying coffee. I did not cancel anything. What I did was open a second account that has no card, and every time somebody paid me I moved a small amount into it before I looked at the balance. Small. Painless. I forgot it existed for about nine months. Then one afternoon I opened it and there was enough for the flight, and I booked it in twenty minutes, before I could think about it. That is the part I recommend. Do not decide when you have time to be sensible. And now I am doing it again, for a longer trip, and this time I know it works.

There is a difference between a plan and a dream, and I learned it late. A dream is a sentence. A plan has a date in it. For eleven years I said I was going to learn to sail. Eleven years. I said it at parties, I said it to my wife, I probably said it to you. And nothing ever happened, because the sentence never had a Tuesday in it. Then last March somebody asked me when, and I did not have an answer, and it embarrassed me enough that I booked a course for the following month. Six lessons. I was the oldest person on the boat by about twenty years and I did not care at all. So here is my only advice. Keep the dream, but put a date on it this week, and tell somebody, because a promise you make out loud is much harder to move.

Two things people forget every single year, and both of them are boring, which is exactly why they forget. The first one is the passport. Look at yours today, before you read anything else. A lot of countries will not let you in if it expires within six months, so a passport that is valid until March is not valid for a trip in January. The second one is the ticket. When you book, the name has to match the passport exactly, every letter, including the middle name you never use. If it does not, some airlines will change it for free in the first twenty-four hours, and after that they will charge you more than the ticket cost. Neither of these is interesting. Both of them will save you a very bad morning at an airport.
